summary: Dedicated GPU pool attach thinness during midday burst caused by long-lived embedding writer
description:
Issue summary:
During a midday burst (11:40–12:10 UTC) the customer's dedicated pool in us-east experienced a sudden attach thinness: new inference attaches failed with timeouts and a spike in p99 latency. Customer (NimbusMaps) reported degraded throughput for both embeddings and short generation routes.

Impact:
- NimbusMaps (dedicated customer) saw ~70% reduction in successful attach rate for short-lived connections and a p99 latency increase from ~220ms -> ~2.8s for embedding requests.
- Platform autoscaler delayed scale-up by ~90s due to noisy telemetry aggregation. Other tenants in the same reserved pool observed transient p50 degradation.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool: reserved-pool-usc-east-7a (GPU A100s mixed NVLink)
- Customer plan: reserved monthly; pinned model open-embed-2.1 and redwood-3b-quant-v2 for some routes

Steps to reproduce (observed in telemetry):
1) Customer started a large batched embedding job with 100 concurrent short streams at ~11:35 UTC across 10 worker processes.
2) Several of these streams created long-lived pinned KV caches due to repetitive long-context inputs (>= 4k tokens) and prefetch hints in SDK v2.3.1.
3) New attach requests during the burst were queued; some timed out with 504s from the attach proxy.
4) Autoscaler metric window aggregated noisy heartbeats from sidecars and suppressed scale decision until the next smoothing window (~90s later).

Observed behavior:
- Attach timeouts (attach proxy 504) and attach latency spikes in scheduler logs.
- A small cohort of connections held persistent GPU slot reservations via a long-lived prefetch cycle (observed by slot-tracker logs).
- Telemetry sidecar emitted high-frequency heartbeat metrics (50–200/s per sidecar) which overwhelmed the autoscaler rate-limiter and led to delayed reactions.

Expected behavior:
- Autoscaler should recognize sustained attach failure and trigger scale-up or fallback in <30s.
- Long-lived streams should not prevent fair attach distribution across the reserved pool.

Initial mitigation applied:
- Support temporarily increased attach proxy timeout to 8s for the customer's routes and bumped autoscaler smoothing sensitivity for the pool.
- SRE evicted two long-lived slot reservations identified in slot-tracker (manual eviction) to free slots for pending attaches.

Notes on customer impact and business risk:
- Customer reported reduced embeddings throughput at a high-traffic time for a product demo. Risk to renewal if recurrence occurs.
comments: 2026-03-13 12:05 - Maya Chen (Support): Triage: customer called in. Confirmed attach timeouts and increased error rate on embed routes. Logged initial mitigation with SRE escalation.

2026-03-13 12:12 - Diego Martinez (SRE): Investigating slot-tracker and prefetch logs. Found 3 long-running sessions holding KV cache >45m. Manual eviction scheduled for two sessions; third flagged for graceful drain.
2026-03-13 12:25 - NimbusMaps (Customer): Confirmed partial recovery after eviction. Throughput improved but intermittent p99 remains elevated. Asked for root cause and permanent fix.

2026-03-13 13:00 - Elena Park (Platform Eng): Observed autoscaler heartbeat saturation in telemetry. Sidecar heartbeat burst correlated with SDK change: SDK v2.3.1 enabled aggressive prefetching by default. Opening a follow-up engineering task.

2026-03-14 09:10 - Diego Martinez (SRE): Added temporary rate-limit on sidecar heartbeat ingestion for reserved-pool-usc-east-7a to prevent autoscaler suppression while a permanent fix is implemented.

2026-03-14 11:30 - Maya Chen (Support): Scheduled customer sync and shared temporary mitigations and planned timeline for engineering fix. Customer requested postmortem and timeline before EOD 2026-03-16.
investigation_notes: Slot-tracker logs show 3 sessions with persistent slot reservations: session_ids s-5781, s-5782, s-5783; s-5781 and s-5782 were evicted at 11:48 UTC.
Autoscaler metrics: heartbeat_ingest_rate spiked to 1.6k/s for pool window; smoothing window prevented scale-up because noise exceeded threshold for burst detector.
Prefetch behavior: SDK v2.3.1 prefetch auto-enabled when input pattern includes long-context markers; this produced repeated KV cache growth without releasing slots.
Scheduler traces: attach queue length rose from 2 -> 110 in ~90s; attach proxy started returning 504 after queue hit configured max_wait.

Telemetry pipeline: sidecar flood bypassed local debounce because of a malformed batch encoding introduced in sidecar v1.12. Confirmed in sidecar logs: repeated POST /heartbeat with identical payload IDs.
Potential root causes: aggressive SDK prefetch + malformed sidecar batching + autoscaler smoothing parameters too conservative for this failure mode.
Risk vector: repeated long-context embedding jobs from any tenant could reproducibly trigger the same attach-thinness if not mitigated platform-side.
resolution: Workarounds and fixes in progress: 1) Rolling deploy of a sidecar patch (v1.12.1) to fix batching and add local debounce (PR #6420). 2) Autoscaler tuning: reduce smoothing window for reserved pools during attach-failure events (config change). 3) SDK advisory and hotfix to change default prefetching behavior for embedding routes (coord with developer relations). Customer notified; SRE applied short-term heartbeat rate-limit. Postmortem and permanent remediation targeted by 2026-03-16.
next_steps: 1) Complete sidecar patch rollout to all reserved pools (target 2026-03-15 18:00 UTC). 2) Autoscaler config change validated in staging and schedule production push. 3) Draft SDK advisory and release patch with guidance to disable aggressive prefetch for large embedding batches. 4) Postmortem with customer and update runbook to detect heartbeat floods earlier.
